cases.question: When you generate a job report with site visits are the site visit field notes supposed to appear on the job report too?
cases.july_answer_text:
No — *site visit field notes are not expected to automatically appear on a generated job/work order report.* Prior internal answers on this exact question say job reports pull from the *job* record, while *site visit notes are stored on the separate site visit record* and don’t flow into the job report by default. [MEM-4]

That lines up with internal docs showing *site visits are a subcomponent of a job*, not the same record. [INT-1] The public docs also only confirm job reports can show job-level notes/details/photos, and separately say site visit notes are used in site visit reporting or can be inserted into estimates/invoices — not job reports. [HC-1]

If someone needs those notes in a PDF, the current workaround has been to use a *site visit-specific output/workflow* rather than the job report. [MEM-1]

cases.question:
Do we integrate with "Intuit Suite"? erp.intuit.com (https://erp.intuit.com/)

Prospect is moving from QBD to the above Jan 1. Have never heard of Intuit Suite
cases.july_answer_text:
Yes — if they mean *Intuit Enterprise Suite (IES)*, we *do* integrate with it via the *QuickBooks Online* integration path, not the QuickBooks Desktop one. [MEM-1]

The main caveat is that IES rides on the QBO API, so standard QBO sync behavior should work, but any *IES-specific features beyond the QB financial layer* may not be supported/documented yet. [MEM-1] If they’re moving from *QBD to IES on Jan 1*, the recommended path is to let Intuit complete the QBD→QBO/IES conversion first, verify the migrated data, and *then* connect FieldPulse to the final account once — connecting to QBD now and converting later can create duplicate sync issues. [INT-1]

One more gotcha: if they plan to use IES’s umbrella/multi-entity structure, FieldPulse multi-location still requires *2+ separate QB entities*. [MEM-2]

cases.question: is there a word limit for invoice notes
cases.july_answer_text:
There’s *no word limit* for invoice notes — it’s a *character limit*. Invoice notes in FieldPulse allow up to *10,000 characters*. [INT-1]

If the invoice syncs to QuickBooks, the effective limit is lower:
- *QuickBooks Online:* 1,000 characters for the customer-facing invoice note. [HC-3]
- *QuickBooks Desktop:* 4,095 characters. [HC-4]

If they mean *internal invoice notes* specifically, team knowledge says those don’t have a FieldPulse limit, but QBO truncates synced internal notes at *4,000 characters*. [MEM-1]

cases.question: can you collect payment on offline mode?
cases.july_answer_text:
No — *payment collection is not available in Offline Mode.* You can still view cached payment records on an invoice, preview invoices/estimates, collect signatures, and update invoice status, but you’ll need to reconnect to the internet before taking a payment. [INT-1]

If the real issue is the *Partner Payments* tab spinning forever, that’s separate from offline mode — the offline docs don’t list a special loading prerequisite beyond being online. [INT-1]

cases.question:
Hi team, did we remove the toggle option for including Wisetack as a payment option?
Are qualified invoices now automatically showing the Wisetack financing option, or is there still a way for users to manually enable or disable Wisetack on a per-invoice basis?
cases.july_answer_text:
Yes — the *per-invoice/per-estimate Wisetack toggle was removed*. That control now exists for *Acorn only*; Wisetack does *not* have a manual enable/disable option on individual documents. Only one financing integration can be enabled at a time. [MEM-1]

For Wisetack, the behavior is now automatic: if Wisetack is enabled on the account, it shows on *qualifying* estimates and invoices rather than being manually toggled per document. Qualification is *residential customers* and *$500–$25,000*; commercial customers or out-of-range amounts will not show the financing option. [MEM-4]

One gotcha: the Wisetack financing link is *customer-facing only*, so the FP user may not see it in their own preview the way they expect. [MEM-3]

There is no current per-document workaround — the only control today is effectively at the *account level* by enabling/disabling Wisetack for the business. [MEM-2]

cases.question: Are FP Payments/Rainforest emails sent to founding user only or is it to all admins?
cases.july_answer_text:
It *depends on the email type*:

- *Most FP Payments / Rainforest emails go to all admins* — including successful payment, deposit/funds deposited, and card charged notifications. There’s currently *no UI or notification setting* to limit those recipients. [MEM-8]
- *ACH return emails are the exception* — those go to the *founding admin* rather than all admins. [MEM-2]
- Chargeback / dispute action emails are sent by FieldPulse based on Rainforest webhooks. [INT-1]

If the ask is “can this be changed?”, the current answer is *no* — turning notification settings on/off in FieldPulse doesn’t stop these, and changing recipients would need a feature request. [MEM-4]

cases.question: if customer communications are enabled with triggers and customer has engage, will it send from a no reply number or the engage number?
cases.july_answer_text:
It depends on the *Send Customer Communication via Engage Account* toggle.

- *If ON*: trigger-based customer communications send from an *Engage number*, not the no-reply toll-free number. Which Engage line gets used depends on the routing setup: Smart SMS Delegation uses the assigned user’s line, then the owner’s, then another available Engage line if needed. [HC-1]
- *If OFF*: they send from the generic FieldPulse *no-reply* number, even if the customer/account has Engage enabled. [MEM-3]

So *having Engage alone isn’t enough* — the toggle has to be enabled for those automated messages to come from Engage. [HC-1]

cases.question: Is there anyway we can opt someone back in for communications through FieldPulse?
cases.july_answer_text:
No — if they opted out of SMS by replying *STOP*, you *cannot* opt them back in from FieldPulse. They have to re-subscribe themselves by texting *START* from their own number. Re-checking SMS in Notification Settings will not override the opt-out. [INT-1]

While they’re opted out, *all* SMS from FieldPulse is blocked — automated notifications, one-off texts, and links sent by SMS, including Engage messages. You can still contact them by *email or phone*. [INT-1]

cases.question: , when using the material list as the inventory deduction method, does the material list have to be in the completed status for the inventory to actually be removed?
cases.july_answer_text:
Yes — if the inventory deduction method is set to *Material List*, inventory is only removed when the material list reaches *Completed* status. [INT-1]

Until it’s completed, inventory is *not* deducted yet. Once the material list is completed, the deduction is applied and the setting locks; if the record is moved back to *Draft*, the inventory is returned and the toggle becomes editable again. [HC-1]

cases.question: Can we change font size in the app
cases.july_answer_text:
No — there isn’t an *in-app* setting to change font size in FieldPulse web or mobile. [HC-1]

Font size follows the *device or browser settings* instead, so the workaround is to adjust:
- *iPhone/iPad* text size in iOS settings [HC-1]
- *Android* font/display size in device settings [HC-1]
- *Chrome* page zoom or browser appearance settings [HC-1]

If they mean *PDFs* specifically, estimate/invoice font size is handled separately in the PDF settings rather than as a global app font setting. [HC-2]

Confluence didn’t return anything useful here, so the help center answer is the best current source. [HC-1]

cases.question: should we be able to take payments offline?
cases.july_answer_text:
No — *payments cannot be collected offline*. Offline Mode lets users view cached invoice/payment info and make some invoice updates, but *payment collection is unavailable until the device reconnects to the internet*. [INT-1]

The public docs say the same thing: you can still preview invoices, collect signatures, and update certain statuses offline, but not take a payment. [HC-1]

cases.question: Why can I not see the option to choose a status workflow when creating a new job?
cases.july_answer_text:
The *Custom Status Workflow* dropdown only shows on job creation if the account already has *more than one* workflow available. If they only have the default workflow, there’s nothing to choose from, so the option won’t appear. [HC-2]

What to check:
- Go to *Company Settings → Jobs → Custom Status* and confirm at least one additional custom workflow has been created and saved. [HC-1]
- If this is a franchise account, note that *only the franchisor can update workflows*, so the location may be visible but not editable by the franchisee. [INT-1]
- If they expected a prebuilt workflow to exist, the account may still need a workflow template imported. Templates are imported from *Master → ClearPath Import*. [INT-2]

If multiple workflows already exist and the dropdown still isn’t showing, I couldn’t find another documented cause in internal docs. [HC-1]

cases.question: how to setup in Engage, "Your call is been recorded" for outbound calls?
cases.july_answer_text:
Yes — that announcement is controlled at the *phone line* level in Engage, not per user or per individual outbound call. [HC-1]

*To turn on “your call is being recorded” for outbound calls:*
1. Go to *Engage > Settings > Phone Numbers*. [HC-1]
2. Open the phone number/line you want to update. [HC-1]
3. Turn on *Record Calls*. [HC-1]
4. Make sure *Play audio to inform the customer of the recorded call* is turned *On*. [HC-1]

With those two settings enabled, Engage will record *both inbound and outbound calls* on that line and play the recording notice automatically. [HC-1] This setting is documented as *on by default*. [HC-2]

Internal docs didn’t add anything more specific on outbound announcement setup beyond the help center steps.

cases.question: Is CFR available for fullstack?
cases.july_answer_text:
Yes — *Card Fee Recovery is available for Full Stack Payments* users. Internal docs explicitly list it as available to *FieldPulse Payments (Rainforest) customers in the US, CardConnect, and Full Stack Payments users*, and *not available for Canadian or Australian accounts*. [INT-1]

The public docs are consistent with that: CFR is available through *Partner Payments*, and *Fullstack* is one of the supported partner processors. [HC-1]

cases.question: where to check cost basis in reporting?
cases.july_answer_text:
If they mean *standard reporting*, send them to the *Invoice Cost Basis & Profit Margin* report and make sure the *Cost Basis* column is enabled. [HC-3]

If they mean *job-level costing/reporting*, that’s in *Job Costing* — either on the *Job > Cost* tab or in the *Job Costing* report. It has broader cost data than the invoice cost basis view and is configured under *Company Settings > Jobs > Job Costing*. [INT-2]

One gotcha: users with *Limited* or *Service Agent* roles can’t see Job Costing, and Team Managers only see it if an admin grants permission. [INT-2]
